newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan dealers group attacks MOF eurobond tax plan.
newsitem.headline: Japan dealers group attacks MOF eurobond tax plan.

text.p: The Japan Securities Dealers' Association (JSDA) has urged the Ministry of Finance (MOF) to modify its plan requiring frequent identification of holders of foreign bonds issued by Japanese firms, including eurobonds, a JSDA official said on Wednesday.

"MOF's Tax Bureau plan is not going to work. If MOF goes ahead with the plan as it is, Japanese issuers will stop issuing foreign bonds. This would lead to a vicious cycle of less liquidity and higher issue costs," a JSDA official said.
MOF's plan is to require that a custodian of foreign bonds issued by Japanese firms identify the bond holder each time a coupon payment is made.
The contentious scheme reflects MOF's long-standing desire to close a tax loophole.
MOF allows a tax break on income gains on foreign bonds, including eurobonds, issued by Japanese firms and held by non-residents of Japan.
However, according to MOF, local investors have used the tax break intended for foreign holders to avoid paying taxes.
A MOF study showed that 70 percent to 80 percent of such bonds are held by Japanese investors.
The JSDA's counterproposal would require that the holder be identified only at the time the bond is sold by the underwriting broker, and that the broker be responsible for the identification.

MOF said in May that it had softened its stance from last October when it first announced a plan to totally scrap the tax exemption and introduce a new rule requiring investors in foreign bonds to identify themselves.
But the JSDA official said that MOF's new plan was still not feasible.
MOF wants to finalise the identification rule by the end of June and to enact the new legislation in time for an extraordinary parliament session in the autumn, industry sources said.
